practices.why: An env file holds credentials and local settings. Tracked, it reaches every clone and stays in the history for good; a lane environment's written files must be ignored too.
practices.fix: Add `.env`, `.env.*`, and `!.env.example` to `.gitignore`. For a tracked env file, run `git rm --cached <path>` and rotate every credential it held.

practices.why: A credential in a tracked file or in history can be read by anyone who can read the repository, every lane included, and deleting the file does not remove it from history.
practices.fix: Revoke and rotate the credential at its provider first, then remove it from the file. Removing it from history needs a history rewrite, which ropeshift does not do. Acknowledge a match that is a test fixture or an example.

practices.why: Checks on every change catch what a review misses, and with review target `pull_request` the base branch's required checks gate the merge.
practices.fix: Add a GitHub Actions workflow that runs the repository's checks and make its check required on the base branch (https://docs.github.com/en/actions/concepts/workflows-and-actions/workflows). With no CI, follow the no-CI recipe: a pre-commit hook and merge authority `person_merges` or `person_approves`.

practices.why: A quick check before every commit, each lane's commit included, catches errors before they reach a review.
practices.fix: Commit the pre-commit configuration, or in a workspace keep the `Makefile`'s `hooks` target and run `make hooks`.

practices.why: Without a lockfile each install can resolve different versions, so a build cannot be repeated and a compromised release can enter unseen.
practices.fix: Run the manager's lock command and commit the file it writes.

practices.fix: Choose a license and commit it as `LICENSE` (https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/managing-your-repositorys-settings-and-features/customizing-your-repository/licensing-a-repository).
